messages:
ada-support: Customer ticket #C-6721 — customer reports intermittent websocket streaming stalls when connected from their corporate network through a VPC NAT + outbound proxy. They see the first ~1-2 KB of tokens immediately, then a long silence (5-30s) where no chunks arrive, then either a burst of the remaining chunks or the socket closes. They say this happens only from their office network, mobile works fine. Logs show occasional 'write: broken pipe' on our side.

sam: Thanks, adding team. Do we have any pcap or timestamps from the client side? Which proxy/NAT in front of them? Any TLS inspection boxes?

customer-acct-42: We uploaded a pcap to the provided link: https://s3.company.internal/c-6721/pcap.pcapng. Environment notes: egress goes through Palo Alto NGFW + a corporate HTTP forward proxy that does TLS break/inspect for some destinations (not all). They use a NAT Gateway in their VPC. All egress allowed only to port 443.

kai: I pulled the pcap. Observations: the websocket upgrade completes fine. Server sends several small TLS records totaling ~12–18KB quickly, then nothing for ~20s. After ~20s the proxy releases a buffered chunk and we see another burst. No TCP retransmits during silence, and TCP connection remains ESTABLISHED. That pattern suggests the middlebox/proxy is coalescing TLS records and delaying send (buffering) until either idle timeout or some internal buffer threshold.

ingrid: Additional theory: some HTTP forward proxies buffer outbound TLS payloads when they classify traffic as long-lived streaming to try to optimize TLS-inspection. If the proxy expects HTTP responses with a Content-Length it may hold on to data. Websockets should be passthrough after upgrade, but misconfig or old proxy firmware can accidentally rebuffer frames.

sam: Repro requests for the customer: can you try a direct connection from a machine that bypasses corp proxy (e.g., cellular hotspot) and paste timings? Also if you can run a quick websocat session and capture the client-side timing that helps. Example test command:

```
# simple websocket test with wscat (npm install -g wscat)
wscat -c wss://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
# then trigger a long streaming response and note when initial bytes vs later bytes arrive
```

customer-acct-42: Confirmed — hotspot bypass works fine, continuous stream. On corporate network we see the drip behavior and sometimes the socket eventually closes after ~35s. We've shared the pcap and a short tcpdump from client.

kai: Quick mitigations to try on our side while they investigate proxy config: 1) add periodic websocket-level pings from server every 10s to keep the proxy's internal idle timers active (not ideal but low-effort). 2) enable TCP_NODELAY and reduce write coalescing to push smaller TLS records more frequently. 3) offer them a private egress IP allowlist so their proxy can whitelist our IPs and avoid inspection for that traffic (if their security policy allows).

eng-runtime-oncall: Note that enabling TCP_NODELAY can increase packet rate; check batching/throughput impacts. We should also check our runtime's TLS record sizing logic — some TLS stacks naturally coalesce application writes into fewer TLS records which some middleboxes then buffer.

ingrid: If they are using nginx/varnish in front of the proxy chain, set proxy_buffering off or reduce proxy_buffer_size. For managed devices (Palo Alto/GW) they will need to adjust SSL Forward Proxy settings to exclude websocket endpoints from decryption or increase the streaming flush interval. For AWS ALB: ALB's idle timeout default is 60s (not likely the issue here) but ALB can buffer in some edge cases if used with certain target groups.

sam: Can we collect a snippet of server-side logs (request id + times of send frames) so we can correlate with pcap bursts? If we have exact request_id I can add correlation. Also asking security for an allowlist exception path.

customer-acct-42: Provided request-id: r-20260305-9b3c and uploaded server logs to the same bucket. They tried adding an outbound rule to bypass the forward proxy for the test machine and stream became continuous.

ada-support: Action items: - sam to coordinate allowlist/exception request with customer's security team. - eng-runtime-oncall to review TLS record sizing and consider small-change toggles (tcp_nodelay, min chunk size) as temporary flag. - customer to escalate to their firewall/appliance vendor to disable buffering for websocket endpoints or exempt our domain from SSL Forward Proxy.

support-bot: NOTE: created escalation ticket ES-9209 assigned to eng-runtime-oncall with high priority.

sam: Thanks all — we'll follow up after security team confirms whether an allowlist is possible. If they cannot change proxy, we'll pilot server-side periodic pings + tcp_nodelay as a temporary mitigation and monitor for CPU/packet overhead. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
